subject: Luma Analytics: multi-year prepay — year-split invoicing & rev-rec coordination
messages:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@luma-analytics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: finance@luma-analytics.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Question on invoicing cadence for 3-year prepay

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the proposal — the team is excited about Redwood. Quick question from our finance side as we prepare the purchase order: can we have the 3-year prepay invoiced as a split across our fiscal years (FY27 / FY28 / FY29) instead of a single upfront invoice?

Specifically: we want Year 1 (partial FY27) to be ~45% of the total, Year 2 ~35%, Year 3 ~20%. From a procurement and cashflow perspective we prefer staged invoices tied to our fiscal budgeting.

Two asks:
- Is Redwood able to issue legally valid invoices split this way against a single SOW/commitment?
- Any implications we should be aware of for revenue recognition or contract language? Our accounting team wants to understand whether this requires special wording in the SOW or an amendment.

I can loop in our procurement lead if helpful.

Best,
Elaine Park
CFO, Luma Analytics
elaine@luma-analytics.com

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@luma-analytics.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question on invoicing cadence for 3-year prepay

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear note and the percentages. Short answer: yes, we can accommodate split invoicing against a single 3-year commitment.

High level:
- Redwood can issue multiple invoices tied to one SOW/contract (we typically record the commitment in our systems and issue invoices per the agreed schedule).
- From a billing system perspective we will generate separate invoices with references to the master PO/SOW number; payments will reduce the outstanding prepay balance.
- For revenue recognition, standard approach is to recognize revenue over time according to the service period; however the split of invoicing vs. service period can affect timing for both parties.

Im looping in Karthik (finance) and Rafael (revenue ops) to confirm the recommended invoice split we should send on our side and whether we need a short contract amendment or an invoice schedule appendix.

Attachment: SOW_Luma_Redwood_v3.pdf (draft SOW we have on file)

I will come back with a proposed invoice schedule and proposed contract language by end of week.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 08:34:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Luma — need invoice schedule + rev-rec check

Team,

Luma (DL-78345) has asked to split their 3-year prepay across FY27/FY28/FY29 with the following desired weights: ~45% / 35% / 20%. Ive attached the draft SOW and a quick proforma invoice_schedule_proforma.xlsx.

Please advise on two things:
1) From Redwoods billing & tax side — any constraints on issuing three invoices tied to one SOW/commitment? (e.g., tax reporting, PO matching, invoice references)
2) From revenue recognition — if we invoice as split but the service period is continuous (36 months), do we need an amendment to the SOW to reflect the invoicing cadence, or is an invoice schedule appendix sufficient?

Notes: Luma wants invoices issued on 2027-01-03 (FY27), 2028-01-03 (FY28), 2029-01-03 (FY29). They also requested that the FY27 invoice be for 45% of the committed amount.

I think we can support this operationally, but want to confirm accounting treatment and whether Rafaels team prefers different split percentages for rev-rec smoothing. Rafael, can you propose the invoice split youd record for another SaaS-style prepay? Karthik, any tax or AR/cash-application caveats?

Thanks,
Monica

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, rafael_mendes@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Internal: Luma — need invoice schedule + rev-rec check

Monica — quick thoughts below (quoting your note):

1) Billing/tax: OK to issue multiple invoices tied to the same SOW/PO. We should ensure each invoice contains:
   - Master SOW number / PO number
   - Invoice sequence (Invoice 1 of 3, etc.)
   - Clear service period on each invoice (e.g., Invoice 1 covers 2027-01-03 to 2028-01-02 prorated if needed)
   - Tax treatment: no special VAT complication here for US entity; if Luma had an EU entity we'd need VAT handling.

2) Revenue recognition: because this is a single prepaid commitment for services delivered over 36 months, under ASC 606 (our policy) we should recognize revenue over time as the service is delivered. The split of cash receipts (45/35/20) does not change revenue recognition if the service period is continuous. However: 
   - If Luma requests that the FY27 invoice correspond to a shorter service window (e.g., billing Year 1 for a partial period) that *could* affect the allocation.
   - Recommended operational approach: keep the service period as 36 months in the SOW, but add an "Invoice Schedule" appendix that lists amounts and invoice dates. That avoids a formal amendment to material terms.

Rafael, my suggestion for internal recording: we can accept Lumas requested 45/35/20 split. For internal reporting we will: record the total deferred revenue at contract inception and amortize it monthly over 36 months. Cash receipts will be applied against the deferred balance as invoices get paid.

If legal wants to be extra cautious, we can attach the schedule as an appendix and add one sentence to the SOW: "Invoices may be issued per the Invoice Schedule attached to this SOW." That should be enough for procurement and auditors.

Happy to chat if someone wants to walk through the entries.

-Karthik
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@luma-analytics.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Final: Invoice schedule & next steps for SOW DL-78345

Hi Elaine — thanks for the patience while we validated internally. Confirming the approach below and next steps so procurement/accounting at Luma can proceed: 

1) Invoicing cadence (per Luma request):
   - Invoice 1 (Invoice #1001): 45% of total — to be issued 2027-01-03
   - Invoice 2 (Invoice #1002): 35% of total — to be issued 2028-01-03
   - Invoice 3 (Invoice #1003): 20% of total — to be issued 2029-01-03

2) Contract mechanics:
   - We will add a one-page "Invoice Schedule" appendix to the SOW that lists the dates and percentages. No other commercial term changes are required. Wording we propose: "Invoices may be issued per the Invoice Schedule attached to this SOW; total consideration remains unchanged and revenue will be recognized over the 36-month service period."

3) Revenue recognition: Karthik confirmed we will record total deferred revenue at contract start and amortize monthly across 36 months; the invoicing timing does not change revenue allocation.

4) Attachments/links:
   - final_invoice_schedule.xlsx (attached)
   - Draft SOW with appendix added (SOW_Luma_Redwood_v3.pdf)
   - DocuSign link to sign the SOW + invoice schedule: https://docusign.com/link/to/DocuSignEnvelope12345

If that all looks good I will send the DocuSign package to your procurement lead today. Please reply if you prefer different invoice numbering or need us to match a specific PO reference format.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this live with Luma.

Best,
Monica Patel
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
